primitives.name: Runner-Tackler Determination Dynamics
primitives.verbatim_quote: The runner must have the determination to get away and keep on advancing the ball and the tackler must have the firm resolution that his opponent must not be allowed to go a step further.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'D_r': "runner's determination (dimensionless)", 'D_t': "tackler's determination (dimensionless)", 'F_r': "runner's forward force (N)", 'F_t': "tackler's resistance force (N)"}
primitives.assumptions: Both players act with maximal effort; forces are conservative and deterministic within a given moment.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When D_r < D_t, runner fails to advance; when F_r < F_t, tackler succeeds.

The core of football lies in the interplay between two opposing forces—runner and tackler—each driven by distinct yet interdependent motivations. This dynamic is best captured through a deterministic game-theoretic lens where each player’s action is a response to the other’s. The runner's determination (D_r) and the tackler's determination (D_t) form a binary conflict, with outcomes governed by the relative strength of their resolve. In this context, judgment (J) becomes a critical variable that modulates how quickly and accurately a player adapts to changing conditions. As situations evolve, the complexity (S) of the environment increases, demanding higher-order adaptability (A_s), which is quantified by the number of possible maneuvers (M) available to the player. Strategic variety (V) emerges as a key performance indicator, reflecting the player’s ability to vary tactics across scenarios. These primitives form a layered system where lower-level determinism gives way to higher-level cognition, enabling real-time tactical evolution. The failure mode occurs when static strategies are applied to dynamic environments, leading to predictable outcomes and loss of competitive edge.
